note: REGRESSION GUARD for a defect this tool found in ITSELF, in production, on the branch that added the derived half. A devlog PR titled 'journal: … a declaration now reaches it (quince#87)' was scanned with a naive `#[0-9]+`, deriving quince-devlog#87 — a CROSS-REPO reference resolved against the wrong repository, which is devlog#18's exact class reproduced mechanically. It surfaced as `event=issue-fetch-failed repo=novkostya/quince-devlog issue=87 reason=GraphQL:_Could_not_resolve_to_an_issue…`, the tool answering correctly a question it should never have asked. `quince#87` is quince's, and a repo-qualified reference is exactly the one a per-repo fetch must not claim. This fixture carries NO issue payloads, so the stub errors if any issue is fetched at all — a regression therefore shows up as an `issue-fetch-failed` line that the expectation does not contain, rather than as a silent extra call. It is a loop fixture rather than a pair because the derivation lives in tick()'s impure half, which only the real verb reaches; expressing it at all needed the stub's second queue, which is the `"kind": "loop"` gap quince#87 declared as owed.

payloads.title: journal: the escalation channel was unwatched, and a declaration now reaches it (quince#87)
